QASHANI:92:13-17/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:13-17/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:13-17/r1.claim: God owns both lives and gives both to those who turn toward Him; one who chooses the higher necessarily receives the lower as well.
QASHANI:92:13-17/r1.anchor: نعطيهما من توجه إلينا فلا نحرم التارك المجرد عن ثواب الدنيا مع ثواب الآخرة

QASHANI:92:13-17/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:92:13-17/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:92:13-17/r2.claim: A cited verse illustrates that those choosing the higher receive provision from above and beneath.
QASHANI:92:13-17/r2.anchor: لأكلوا من فوقهم ومن تحت أرجلهم

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.claim: Verses 11–14 admonish Quraysh that God guides through revelation but does not force acceptance; they alone benefit from accepting, while both worlds remain under His control.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p343/r6.anchor: this world and the next are in the grasp of God

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r5.claim: God’s responsibility is to guide people through His Messenger, not force them to follow; accepting guidance is their responsibility, and their outcomes follow their choice.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p349/r5.anchor: It is not His responsibility to force this guidance on people. Accepting this guidance is their responsibility.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r1.claim: Both this world and the next are in God’s control; neither personal strategy nor racial status and deities can secure benefit, and everyone faces God alone, as discussed at 53:25.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r1.anchor: achieve anything in this world nor in the next.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r2.claim: The wealthy may credit their riches to their own intelligence, like Qārūn’s claim at 28:78; Islahi says the verse overturns this self-reliant capitalist mentality because all gain comes from God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p350/r2.anchor: in the next is also from God

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r10.claim: God owns the reward of both worlds, as with Abraham's reward in this life and status among the righteous in the next.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p493/r10.anchor: وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى: أي ثواب الدارين، لقوله تعالى:

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r5.claim: The first and last lives belong to God; seeking them from anyone else is taking the wrong path.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p447#2/r5.anchor: {وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى} فمن طلبهما من غير مالكهما فقد أخطأ الطريق.

BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r1.claim: The next life and this life belong to God: He gives what He wills in both, grants the reward of guidance, and is unharmed if people refuse guidance.
BAYDAWI-FULL:92:13-19/r1.anchor: { وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى } فنعطي في الدارين ما نشاء لمن نشاء

BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r4.claim: Both the present and the afterlife belong to God, who alone controls giving and withholding; rejecting His guidance harms only the rejecter.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r4.anchor: فمن ترك ما بينا له من طريق الهداية لم يخرج عن كونه لنا ولم يضر إلا نفسه

BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r5.claim: The afterlife is named before this world for the deniers’ concern, not merely for cadence; the author rejects treating Qur’anic ordering as rhyme or poetic meter.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p448/r5.anchor: فقد ثبت بطلان هذا وأنه لا يحل اعتقاده في غير موضع , منها آخر سورة براءة

NAHHAS:v5p243/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p243/r1.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p243/r1.claim: The same emphatic lām construction applies in the adjoining statement about the Hereafter and the first life.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r9.claim: Al-akhirah and al-ula mean the two abodes.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p491#2/r9.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى أن «الآخرة والأولى» أي الدارين.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767#2/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767#2/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767#2/r2.claim: The last and first lives belong to God as reward for the one who follows guidance, as in Abraham's descendants receiving prophecy and scripture.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p767#2/r2.anchor: أي : ثواب الدارين للمهتدي ، كقوله : { ووهبنا له إسحاق ويعقوب

QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r11.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r11.claim: Ata transmitting from Ibn Abbas identifies the hereafter with Paradise and the first life with this world; both belong to God.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r11.anchor: وكذا روى عطاء عن ابن عباس. أي الدنيا والآخرة لله تعالى.

QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r12.speaker: أبو صالح عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r12.claim: Abu Salih transmits Ibn Abbas's interpretation as the reward of this world and the next; seeking either from anyone but its owner misses the way.
QURTUBI-FULL:92:11-13/r12.anchor: وروى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس قال: ثواب الدنيا والآخرة، وهو كقوله تعالى:

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.claim: The sura develops two antitheses: behavior and recompense for the saved and damned, first in verses 5–13 and then in verses 14–21.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es folgen zwei Antithesen (V. 5–13 und V. 14–21), welche die Verhaltensweisen und Jenseitsschicksale von Seligen und Verdammten miteinander kontrastieren

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.speaker: Neuwirth
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.claim: Neuwirth classifies verse 11 with the theological predication in verses 12–13 rather than with the preceding description of the wicked.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r6.anchor: anders Neuwirth, Studien, 229 und Neuwirth, Frühmekkanische Suren, 228

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r8.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r8.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r8.claim: God's self-predication separates the second and third stanzas and serves as a compositional hinge affirming divine power over both worlds and supporting the threats and promises; Cuypers sees it as the sura's center.
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:5-12:kommentar/r8.anchor: Die göttliche Selbstprädikation V. 12.13 setzt das zweite und dritte Gesätz voneinander ab: Sie fungiert als eine kompositorische Fuge

TABRISI:92:5-15/r16.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:5-15/r16.speaker: author
TABRISI:92:5-15/r16.claim: God owns this life and the next; human obedience adds nothing to His dominion and disobedience subtracts nothing.
TABRISI:92:5-15/r16.anchor: ملك الآخرة وملك الأولى فلا يزيد في ملكنا اهتداء من اهتدى ولا ينقص

TABRISI:92:5-15/r17.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:92:5-15/r17.speaker: author
TABRISI:92:5-15/r17.claim: Although God could compel people, moral responsibility requires guidance through explanation, commands, and warnings.
TABRISI:92:5-15/r17.anchor: ولو نشاء لمنعناهم عن ذلك قسرا وجبرا ولكن التكليف اقتضى أن نمنعهم بيانا

THALABI:v10p218/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p218/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p218/r8.claim: The next life and this life both belong to God; seeking them from anyone else is taking the wrong path.
THALABI:v10p218/r8.anchor: وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى فمن طلبها من غير مالكهما فقد أخطأ الطريق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r4.claim: The givers seek the Hereafter, while misers seek worldly life; both the first and last life belong to God, so people should follow His guidance in each.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r4.anchor: لأن الذي يعطي ويتقي يريد الآخرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r5.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r5.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r5.claim: Ease and hardship may occur in this life or the next, both of which belong to God; people should therefore follow what He commands.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p378/r5.anchor: التيسير والتعسير إما أن يكونا في الدنيا أو في الآخرة ولله الآخرة والأولى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.claim: The lām emphasizing God's ownership suits the surah's repeated focus on wealth and possession; unlike this context, the wealth-free context of 53:25 omits it.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r1.anchor: فسياق الآيات في سورة الليل جاء كله في الأموال وامتلاكها والتصرف فيها

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r2.claim: The Qur'an pairs al-ākhirah with al-ūlā, never al-dunyā; al-ūlā is broader, including all earlier affairs of the heavens and earth, whereas al-dunyā denotes human life in this world.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r2.anchor: لم يرد في القرآن الكريم كله ولا مرة واحدة لفظ الدنيا مع الآخرة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r3.claim: Because al-ūlā is broader than al-dunyā, it aptly expresses the breadth of God's ownership in this surah.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p380/r3.anchor: لما أراد الله تعالى أن يذكر سعة الملك في سورة الليل ناسب أن يأتي بكلمة الأولى

ELMALILI:92:12-21/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r3.claim: This life and the afterlife belong entirely to God, with no competing sovereign; no one can escape by dispensing with His guidance, and defying His will harms only themselves.
ELMALILI:92:12-21/r3.anchor: Evvel ü âhir mülk Bizim, hakk-ı tasarruf Bizimdir. Mu‘âraza veya müdahale edecek başka bir mâlik yoktur.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.speaker: Müfessirler
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.claim: Others say verses 5–19 were revealed about Abu Bakr; regardless of a specific occasion, the message and rulings are general.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:17/r2.anchor: bazıları ise 5-19. âyetlerin (bk. Elmalılı, VIII, 5881), müşriklerin işkence ettiği köleleri satın alıp âzat ederek hürriyetlerine kavuşturan Hz. Ebû Bekir hakkında indiğini söylemişlerdir. Âyetler böyle bir özel olay üzerine gelmiş olsa da, hükümleri ve mesajları geneldir

SULAMI:v2p399/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p399/r1.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p399/r1.claim: A wise person regards the afterlife with certainty and the world as a lesson.
SULAMI:v2p399/r1.anchor: قال بعضهم : العاقل من ينظر إلى الآخرة فيشاهدها مشاهدة اليقين

SULAMI:v2p399/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v2p399/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v2p399/r2.claim: Seeking either world from anyone other than its Owner is taking the wrong path.
SULAMI:v2p399/r2.anchor: وقال بعضهم : من طلب الآخرة والدنيا من غير مالكهما فقد اخطأ الطريق

TUSTARI:92:13/r1.author: Sahl al-Tustarī
TUSTARI:92:13/r1.speaker: author
TUSTARI:92:13/r1.claim: The afterlife corresponds to the soul of spirit and the first life to the soul of nature; people are guided toward one or the other.
TUSTARI:92:13/r1.anchor: فالآخرة نفس الروح، والأولى نفس الطبع، يهدي واحد إلى نفس الروح، وآخر إلى نفس الطبع.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r3.claim: The declaration that both lives belong to God completes the reminder that guidance is a favor; all things in both realms are His, so people have no claim upon Him beyond what He grants.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r3.anchor: وعطف { وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى } على جملة : { إن علينا للهدى } تتميم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r4.claim: Recompense in the next life follows God's disclosed ordering; worldly causes and effects are also His arrangement, and whoever neglects its safeguards deserves the consequences.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p388/r4.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة عظيمة إلى أن أمور الجزاء في الأخرى تجري على ما رتبه الله

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#2/r1.claim: Both the present life and the afterlife belong to God, so let people seek them from Him.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p151#2/r1.anchor: وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى أي فليطلبا منا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r3.claim: The first and the last lives both belong to God, who governs them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p421#2/r3.anchor: أي: الجميع ملكنا (1) وأنا المتصرف فيهما.

FARRA:v3p271/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p271/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p271/r6.claim: God owns the reward of both this life and the next.
FARRA:v3p271/r6.anchor:
الحر » ، وهي تقي الحر والبرد.
وقوله جل وعز: وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى

JISHUMI:v10p7444/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r8.claim: Al-Ūlā is feminine of al-awwal and ellipses the first abode, this world; the latter abode is the Resurrection, Paradise, or Fire.
JISHUMI:v10p7444/r8.anchor: والأولى صفة لمحذوف، أي: الدار الأولى، وهي الدنيا

KASHSHAF:92:13/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:92:13/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:92:13/r1.claim: The guided person receives the reward of both abodes, as in the cited example.
KASHSHAF:92:13/r1.anchor: ثواب الدّارين للمهتدي ،   كقوله : { وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r4.speaker: الكلبي والفراء
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r4.claim: They interpret the first and last lives as the rewards of this world and the next.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r4.anchor: ثواب الدنيا والآخرة , قاله الكلبي والفراء

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r5.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r5.claim: He interprets the verse as God's dominion over this world and the next.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r5.anchor: ملك الدنيا وملك الآخرة , قاله مقاتل

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p289/r6.claim: A further reading says God recompenses people in this world and the next.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#14/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#14/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#14/r1.claim: Because the afterlife and present life belong to God, neither misguidance nor guidance benefits Him; alternatively, whoever seeks either from another source has taken the wrong path.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p343#14/r1.anchor: فلا يضرنا ضلال من ضل ولا ينفعنا اهتداء من اهتدى أو أنهما لنا فمن طلبهما من غيرنا

QUTB-ZILAL:92:13/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:92:13/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:92:13/r1.claim: God's ownership encompasses both the afterlife and this first life, leaving those who seek to flee Him nowhere to take refuge.
QUTB-ZILAL:92:13/r1.anchor: فلا يجدون من دونها موئلا : ( وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى )

RAZI:92:13/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:13/r1.speaker: author
RAZI:92:13/r1.claim: One interpretation says God owns all of both worlds; human guidance benefits or harms humans, while coercing them would undo moral testing, so God instead guides by explanation, promise, and warning. Al-Razi says this suits Muʿtazilites.
RAZI:92:13/r1.anchor: ( الأول ) : أن لنا كل ما في الدنيا والآخرة فليس يضرنا ترككم الاهتداء بهدانا

RAZI:92:13/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:92:13/r2.speaker: author
RAZI:92:13/r2.claim: Another interpretation says God owns both abodes and gives them as He wills, so people should seek happiness in both from Him; al-Razi says this fits his own theology.
RAZI:92:13/r2.anchor: أن لنا ملك الدارين نعطي ما نشاء من نشاء

RAZI-FULL:v31p184/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p184/r1.claim: One reading says both abodes belong to God, so human guidance does not affect His dominion; compelling people away from sin would nullify moral responsibility, so He guides through explanation, promises, and warnings.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184/r1.anchor: أن لنا كل ما في الدنيا والآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v31p184/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p184/r2.claim: Another reading says God owns both abodes and grants them to whom He wills, so people should seek both kinds of happiness from Him.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184/r2.anchor: أن لنا ملك الدارين نعطي ما نشاء من نشاء

RAZI-FULL:v31p184/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p184/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p184/r3.claim: Razi says the first interpretation better suits the Muʿtazila and the second his own school.
RAZI-FULL:v31p184/r3.anchor: والأول أوفق لقول المعتزلة ، والثاني أوفق لقولنا

STUDYQURAN:92:13/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:13/r1.speaker: some commentators
STUDYQURAN:92:13/r1.claim: Some read God's ownership of both abodes as referring to their reward, and by implication their worldly and otherworldly punishment as well.
STUDYQURAN:92:13/r1.anchor: Some commentators see this verse as a reference to the reward of the Hereafter and this world

STUDYQURAN:92:13/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:92:13/r2.speaker: Sh
STUDYQURAN:92:13/r2.claim: Others understand the verse to say everything belongs to God and He disposes of it as He wills.
STUDYQURAN:92:13/r2.anchor: Others see this verse as an indication that everything is God’s and He does with it as He wills

TAB-FULL:v24p476#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p476#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p476#2/r1.claim: God owns this world and the next, grants what He wills, guides those He loves to obedience and honor, and abandons others to disobedience and punishment.
TAB-FULL:v24p476#2/r1.anchor: خذلانه من خلقه عن طاعته، فيهينه بمعصيته في الدنيا، ويخزيه بعقوبته عليها في الآخرة

TABATABAI:92:13-16/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r2.claim: God owns both the afterlife and this life, the realms of beginning and return; everything depends on Him in its existence, and ordinary ownership follows from that real ownership.
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r2.anchor: أي عالم البدء وعالم العود فكل ما يصدق عليه أنه شيء فهو مملوك له تعالى بحقيقة الملك

TABATABAI:92:13-16/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r3.claim: Because God owns all things in every respect, no rival can oppose Him, prevent Him, or overcome Him, as other verses affirm.
TABATABAI:92:13-16/r3.anchor: فهو تعالى يملك كل شيء من كل جهة فلا يملك شيء منه شيئا فلا معارض يعارضه ولا مانع يمنعه

ASAD-NOTES:92:12#n7/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:92:12#n7/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:92:12#n7/r1.claim: Human life here and in the hereafter comprises two stages of one continuous entity.
ASAD-NOTES:92:12#n7/r1.anchor: man's life in this world and in the hereafter are but two stages

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p85/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p85/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p85/r1.claim: The two terms mean the two abodes, this world and the next.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p85/r1.anchor: قوله {وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى} يعني الدارين: الدنيا، والآخرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p85/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p85/r2.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p85/r2.claim: The verse means the reward of this world and the Hereafter, as stated in 4:134.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p85/r2.anchor: قال الكلبي: أي ثواب الدنيا والآخرة (¬4)، (كقوله: {فعند الله ثواب الدنيا والآخرة}

WAHIDI-QT:92:13/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:92:13/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:92:13/r1.claim: The present world and the Hereafter both belong to God; seeking them from anyone else is mistaken.
WAHIDI-QT:92:13/r1.anchor: { وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى } فمن طلبهما من غير مالكهما فقد أخطأ

CORPUSCORANICUM:92:13:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:13:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:92:13:anmerkung/r1.claim: For the paired terms al-ākhira and al-ūlā, consult the note to 93:4.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:12/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:12/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:12/r2.claim: Since both worldly and afterlife existence belong to God's governance, people should seek the good of both from Him.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:92:12/r2.anchor: her iki dünyanın kendi yönetiminde olduğunu belirtmekte, dolayısıyla her iki dünyanın iyilik ve güzelliklerini O’ndan istememiz gerektiğini

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p379/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p379/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p379/r3.claim: Al-Qasas places this world first because its surrounding passage recalls worldly blessings and calls for gratitude; mentioning praise and thanks suits that context.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p379/r3.anchor: السياق كله في الدنيا وما أودع الله تعالى من النعم

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p379/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p379/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p379/r4.claim: Al-Layl omits praise, foregrounds God’s ownership of both realms, and therefore begins with the afterlife, as explained above.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p379/r4.anchor: لم يذكر الحمد وقدم الآخرة كما سبق وفصلنا

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p381/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p381/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p381/r1.claim: The word al-dunyā derives from أدنى and can mean nearer, lower, lesser, or inferior; those senses do not suit a passage stressing God’s vast dominion.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p381/r1.anchor: الدنيا نفسها هي مؤنث الأدنى ومن معانيها الأقرب والأخس

ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#2/r1.claim: God exercises complete authority over both worlds and may do as He wills, including the fates of the generous and miserly; alternatively, He owns both realms and rewards guidance, while people's guidance or error affects themselves alone.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p150#2/r1.anchor: أي التصرف الكلي فيهما كيفما نشاء فنفعل ما نشاء من الأفعال التي من جملتها ما ذكرنا فيمن أعطى وفيمن بخل

BINTSHATI:v2p112/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r1.claim: The passage mentions an unnamed interpreter’s concern that a reading undermines moral responsibility and says the interpretation attributed to al-Tabari better fits the wording.
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r1.anchor: ورأى فيه ما يخل بالتكليف. كما نقل ما ذكرنا من تأويل الطبري

BINTSHATI:v2p112/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r2.claim: She rejects al-Zamakhshari’s restriction of the verse to reward in both abodes because the context plainly includes both glad tidings and warning.
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r2.anchor: قصر معنى الآية في تفسير الزمخشري على "ثواب الدارين" يمنعه العموم المستفاد من صريح السياق

BINTSHATI:v2p112/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r3.claim: Without settling the free-will debate, she says God is both origin and destination, provides guidance in worldly life, and people’s response or refusal shapes their final outcome.
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r3.anchor: الله سبحانه إليه المصير كما له المبتدأ. وهو تعالى يهيئ لخلقه في الدنيا طريق الحق والهدى

BINTSHATI:v2p112/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r4.claim: The afterlife is placed before the first life for meaning, not rhyme: it is better and lasting, and its punishment is more severe and enduring.
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r4.anchor: وليس التعلق برعاية الفاصلة هو الذي اقتضى تقديم الآخرة هنا على الأولى

BINTSHATI:v2p112/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r5.claim: The same order appears in al-Duha’s promise to the Prophet and in the threat concerning Pharaoh, where the afterlife precedes the first life.
BINTSHATI:v2p112/r5.anchor: وكذلك قدمت الآخرة على الأولى في سياق البشرى للمصطفى عليه الصلاة والسلام، بآية الضحى

TAB:92:13/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:13/r1.speaker: author
TAB:92:13/r1.claim: God owns all that is in this world and the next, giving to or withholding from whichever creatures He wills.
TAB:92:13/r1.anchor: وإن لنا ملك ما في الدنيا والآخرة

TAB:92:13/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:92:13/r2.speaker: author
TAB:92:13/r2.claim: God grants obedience to whom He wills, honoring them in this life and preparing their reward in the next; He leaves others to disobey and face humiliation and punishment.
TAB:92:13/r2.anchor: أنه يوفق لطاعته من أحب من خلقه

ITQAN:v2p499/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p499/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p499/r1.claim: The non-governing lām of initiation emphasizes a clause and shifts away from sentence-initial position after inna to avoid two successive emphatics; it also makes the imperfect refer to the present.
ITQAN:v2p499/r1.anchor: لام الابتداء وفائدتها أمران توكيد مضمون الجملة ولهذا زحلقوها في باب إن عن صدر الجملة

ITQAN:v2p499/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p499/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p499/r2.claim: The lām of initiation appears with a subject, in predicates of inna, and in its delayed noun construction; examples include لأَنْتُمْ أَشَدُّ رَهْبَةً, إِنَّ رَبِّي لَسَمِيعُ الدُّعَاءِ, and إِنَّ لَنَا لَلْآخِرَةَ.
ITQAN:v2p499/r2.anchor: وتدخل في المبتدأ نحو ﴿ لأنتم أشد رهبة ﴾ وفي خبر إن نحو ﴿ إن ربي لسميع الدعاء ﴾

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p277/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p277/r3.speaker: قائلون
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p277/r3.claim: Some attribute the fronting in “Indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life” to preserving the verse ending.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p277/r3.anchor: وفي التقديم والتأخير، قالوا برعاية الفاصلة في مقل آية الليل: {إن علينا للهدى (12) وإن لنا للآخرة والأولى}

ABUHAYYAN:92:13/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:13/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:13/r1.claim: The afterlife and this world are the rewards of the two abodes, which belong to God.

ABUHAYYAN:92:13/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:92:13/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:92:13/r2.claim: He supports the two-abodes reading with the statement that Abraham was rewarded in this world and is among the righteous in the next.
ABUHAYYAN:92:13/r2.anchor: لقوله تعالى : { وآتيناه أجره في الدنيا وإنه في الآخرة لمن الصالحين }

ALUSI:92:13/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:13/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:13/r1.claim: God has complete disposal over both abodes and may do as He wills, including reward and punishment; alternatively, all they contain belongs to Him, so human guidance or error cannot benefit or harm Him.
ALUSI:92:13/r1.anchor: أي التصرف الكلي فيهما كيفما نشاء فنفعل فيهما ما نشاء من الأفعال

ALUSI:92:13/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:92:13/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:92:13/r2.claim: Whoever is guided benefits himself, while whoever strays bears the loss himself.
ALUSI:92:13/r2.anchor: كما لا يضرنا ضلالكم فمن اهتدى

BAGHAWI:92:13/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:92:13/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:92:13/r1.claim: God owns both the afterlife and this world; whoever seeks them from anyone other than their owner has taken the wrong path.
BAGHAWI:92:13/r1.anchor: فمن طلبهما من غير مالكهما فقد أخطأ الطريق

BAYDAWI:92:13/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:13/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:13/r1.claim: God may give what He wills in both abodes to whomever He wills.
BAYDAWI:92:13/r1.anchor: فنعطي في الدارين ما نشاء لمن نشاء

BAYDAWI:92:13/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:13/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:13/r2.claim: The phrase may refer to the reward for guidance given to those who follow it.

BAYDAWI:92:13/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:92:13/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:92:13/r3.claim: Alternatively, the point is that people's refusal to follow guidance cannot harm God.

BIQAI:92:13/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:13/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:13/r1.claim: After guidance might sound like an obligation on God, this verse asserts His complete dominion over both worlds: the person who rejects guidance harms only himself, and God grants or withholds as He wills.
BIQAI:92:13/r1.anchor: فمن ترك ما بينا له من طريق الهداية لم يخرج عن كونه لنا

BIQAI:92:13/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:13/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:13/r2.claim: The phrase addresses the deniers and asserts that the afterlife and this world belong exclusively to God.
BIQAI:92:13/r2.anchor: أي يا أيها المنكرون خاصاً بنا

BIQAI:92:13/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:92:13/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:92:13/r3.claim: The order gives priority to the afterlife because the deniers need that emphasis, not for rhyme; he rejects arranging revelation solely for rhyme, citing the end of al-Tawba and noting that alternative wordings could also rhyme.

IBNASHUR:92:13/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:13/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:13/r1.claim: The conjunction completes the preceding statement that guidance is God's responsibility and reminds the audience that both abodes belong to Him, including all they contain.
IBNASHUR:92:13/r1.anchor: تتميم وتنبيه على أن تعهد الله لعباده بالهدى فضل منه

IBNASHUR:92:13/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:13/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:13/r2.claim: Since God owns both abodes, He disposes of them as He wills; people have no claim against Him except what He graciously grants, as Q 5:17 states.
IBNASHUR:92:13/r2.anchor: فله التصرف فيهما كيف يشاء فلا يحسبوا أن عليهم حقا على الله تعالى إلا ما تفضل به

IBNASHUR:92:13/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:13/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:13/r3.claim: Rewards in the Hereafter follow the order God established and made known to people.
IBNASHUR:92:13/r3.anchor: أن أمور الجزاء في الأخرى تجري على ما رتبه الله

IBNASHUR:92:13/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:92:13/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:92:13/r4.claim: The world's systems and effects following causes are established by God, who commands people to preserve them and guides them; neglecting them makes a person deserve the consequences.
IBNASHUR:92:13/r4.anchor: وأن نظام أمور الدنيا وترتب مسبباته على أسبابه أمر قد وضعه الله تعالى

IBNATIYYA:92:13/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:92:13/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:92:13/r1.claim: Al-ākhira and al-ūlā refer to the two abodes, the Hereafter and this world.
IBNATIYYA:92:13/r1.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى أن «الآخرة والأولى » أي الدارين .

IBNKATHIR:92:13/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:92:13/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:92:13/r1.claim: Both the Hereafter and the present world belong to God, and He directs them.
IBNKATHIR:92:13/r1.anchor: وقوله : { وَإِنَّ لَنَا لَلآخِرَةَ وَالأولَى } أي : الجميع ملكنا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas answers that the Prophet left only what is between the two covers; Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya gives the same answer. Al-Bukhari alone transmits this report.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r1.anchor: على ابن عباس، فقال له شداد بن معقل: أترك النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من شيء؟ قال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir explains that the report means the Prophet left no inheritable property, supporting it with Amr ibn al-Harith’s statement that he left no money, enslaved person, or other property.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r2.anchor: ومعناه: أنه، عليه السلام، ما ترك مالا ولا شيئا يورث عنه، كما قال عمرو بن الحارث

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r3.speaker: أبو الدرداء
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r3.claim: Abu al-Darda reports the teaching that prophets leave no dinar or dirham as inheritance; they leave knowledge, and whoever takes it receives an abundant share.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r3.anchor: وفي حديث أبي الدرداء: " إن الأنبياء لم يورثوا دينارا ولا درهما، وإنما ورثوا العلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas means by ‘what is between the covers’ the Qur’an; the Sunnah explains and clarifies it, while God’s Book is the primary inheritance. Ibn Kathir links this to 35:32.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r4.anchor: ولهذا قال ابن عباس: وإنما ترك ما بين الدفتين يعني: القرآن، والسنة مفسرة له

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir says the prophets were created to call people toward the Hereafter, not to accumulate worldly goods and pass them on.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r5.anchor: فالأنبياء، عليهم السلام، لم يخلقوا للدنيا يجمعونها ويورثونها، إنما خلقوا للآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r6.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r6.claim: The Prophet states, ‘We are not inherited; what we leave is charity,’ establishing the rule Ibn Kathir discusses.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r6.anchor: ولهذا قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " لا نورث ما تركنا فهو صدقة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r7.speaker: أبو بكر الصديق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r7.claim: Abu Bakr first publicly affirmed this teaching when asked about the Prophet’s inheritance; Ibn Kathir says many Companions accepted his transmission, including Umar, Uthman, Ali, Abbas, Talha, al-Zubayr, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, Abu Hurayra, and Aisha.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p57/r7.anchor: وكان أول من أظهر هذه المحاسن من هذا الوجه أبو بكر الصديق، رضي الله عنه، لما سئل

MAWARDI:92:13/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:13/r1.speaker: الكلبي والفراء
MAWARDI:92:13/r1.claim: Al-Kalbī and al-Farrāʾ take the two lives to mean their rewards in this world and the next.
MAWARDI:92:13/r1.anchor: أحدهما : ثواب الدنيا والآخرة ،   قاله الكلبي والفراء

MAWARDI:92:13/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:13/r2.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI:92:13/r2.claim: Muqātil takes them to mean God's dominion over this world and the next.
MAWARDI:92:13/r2.anchor: الثاني : ملك الدنيا وملك الآخرة ،   قاله مقاتل

MAWARDI:92:13/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:92:13/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI:92:13/r3.claim: Māwardī also suggests that God is the one who recompenses people in both worlds.

NASAFI:92:13/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:13/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:13/r1.claim: Since the present and afterlife belong to God, the misguidance of the lost neither harms Him nor the guidance of the guided benefits Him.
NASAFI:92:13/r1.anchor: فلا يضرنا ضلال من ضل ولا ينفعنا اهتداء من اهتدى

NASAFI:92:13/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:92:13/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI:92:13/r2.claim: Alternatively, both lives are God's; whoever seeks them from another has taken the wrong path.
NASAFI:92:13/r2.anchor: أو أنهما لنا فمن طلبهما من غيرنا فقد أخطأ الطريق

QURTUBI:92:13/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:13/r1.speaker: عطاء عن ابن عباس
QURTUBI:92:13/r1.claim: Ata reports Ibn Abbas interpreting the hereafter as Paradise and the first life as this world.
QURTUBI:92:13/r1.anchor: " للآخرة " الجنة . " والأولى " الدنيا . وكذا روى عطاء عن ابن عباس

QURTUBI:92:13/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:13/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:92:13/r2.claim: Al-Qurtubi concludes that both this world and the hereafter belong to God.

QURTUBI:92:13/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:92:13/r3.speaker: ابن عباس عن أبي صالح
QURTUBI:92:13/r3.claim: Abu Salih reports Ibn Abbas interpreting the phrase as the rewards of this world and the hereafter; whoever seeks them from anyone but their owner has taken the wrong path.
QURTUBI:92:13/r3.anchor: وروى أبو صالح عن ابن عباس قال : ثواب الدنيا والآخرة ، وهو كقوله تعالى : " من كان يريد ثواب الدنيا
